transcript:
Meeting header:
16:00 PST — 2025-02-18 — Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood), Claire (Pelago Head of ML), Marco (Pelago Platform), Sana (Pelago Security), Tom (Product)

Summary (auto): quick scoping to nail success criteria, benchmark plan, and integration path (SDK or OpenAI-compatible).

00:00 Maya: "Okay everyone, thanks for joining — do we have everyone listed?"
00:04 Claire: "Yeah, hi all, thanks. Running a bit behind earlier but all set now."
00:12 Maya: "Goal for today: align on POC success metrics, what you'd like us to run in the benchmarks, and how you want to integrate — SDK directly or hit an OpenAI-style endpoint. Also surface any security blockers."
00:25 Marco: "High level — our app is an internal annotation assistant and a vector search index for notes. Rough traffic: about 3000 inference calls per hour, with peaks up to 9k. Typical prompt sizes: 80-400 tokens, embeddings are separate flow, roughly 6k embedding requests/hour."
00:45 Evan: "Okay that's helpful. For throughput planning we'll want per-request token distribution. Do you have a 90th percentile tokens-per-request?"
00:53 Marco: "p90 is around 320 tokens. p50 is closer to 140. Embeddings payloads are ~1k tokens when we batch documents."
01:15 Jordan: "Noted. For the POC we'll set up two benchmark classes: low-latency assistant calls (short-turn) and batched embedding ingestion. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies plus cost per 1M tokens and throughput sustained over 30-minute windows."
01:35 Claire: "Success criteria for us: p95 assistant latency < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for short-turn calls. For embeddings we want ability to sustain 6k/hour with under 10% CPU/GPU throttling and predictable cost within our budget. If we hit those goals we'll consider moving to Dedicated capacity."
01:58 Tom: "To add, we need structured outputs from the assistant — a JSON schema with fields extracted from the conversation. We also want the tool/function calling pattern so that the model can signal 'call vector-search' or 'call db' and return structured payloads."
02:17 Sana: "Security: any hosted endpoints must support VPC peering or PrivateLink, and we need KMS integration for key management. SOC2 reports helpful. Also, we're doing ISO readiness so audit logs are a must."
02:36 Maya: "We have a Private control plane option and Dedicated capacity. For this POC we can run against hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints in a restricted VPC and provide a sample KMS integration. We'll share SOC2 docs. Is that acceptable?"
02:50 Sana: "Yes, but we'll need to validate the access pattern. Also want confirmation that ephemeral cache content won't be persisted beyond 72 hours unless flagged — that's a policy for regulated records."
03:10 Evan: "About integration: we offer language SDKs (Python/Node/Go) and an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint. Function/tool calling we support via structured JSON responses and a simple function-calling shim; we also have examples for tool orchestration. SDKs have helpers for streaming and structured outputs."
03:36 Marco: "If we use the OpenAI-compatible path, how easy is it to lift-and-shift our existing client code?"
03:42 Evan: "Very straightforward — same request shapes. Auth is API key; we can provide a proxy example for headers and higher-level helper functions for tool calling. Caveat: small differences in streaming framing and a couple of param names; we'll provide a compatibility guide."
03:58 Jordan: "For benchmarking, we plan two tracks: 1) run a hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint with your prompt set to measure latency and cost; 2) run an on-dedicated node test to show best-case throughput and variance. We'll record token counts, GPU utilization, and kernel-level stalls if any (SE will capture logs)."
04:25 Claire: "What about quantization? We use some smaller models for assistant light tasks and larger models for complex reasoning. Does Redwood supply quantized variants in Dedicated?"
04:33 Evan: "Yes, we can run int8/int4 variants depending on model support. We'll recommend quantization profiles in the 'Optimize' phase after initial benchmarks. But for the POC we'll stick to the same model family to make apples-to-apples comparisons."
04:54 Tom: "Timeline? We were hoping to have a decision point by mid-April because of upcoming product launch."
05:00 Maya: "Sounds doable. Proposed timeline: benchmark harness + quickstart shared by 02/21, customer provides prompts and traffic profile by 02/20, initial hosted runs week of 02/24, Dedicated benchmark week of 03/03, two-week window for tuning + security review, decision meeting mid-April (target 04/14)."
05:24 Claire: "Works for us, subject to Sana's security checks. Also need a demo of function calling with a small end-to-end example."
05:36 Evan: "We'll include a demo repo showing function calling (vector search + DB lookup) and structured JSON responses in both SDK and OpenAI-compat samples."
05:50 Sana: "One more ask: can you provide acting audit log samples and retention controls?"
05:55 Maya: "Yes, we'll share log samples and the console screenshots for retention settings. We'll also include the security whitepaper link."
06:08 Marco: "Benchmark details: for assistant flows we need to measure cold-start vs warm (KV cache) — we saw cold p95 blow up on our current infra. Can you capture cache hit/miss stats?"
06:20 Evan: "Absolutely. We'll instrument KV cache hit rate, batching size distribution, and end-to-end response time; we'll publish the harness as a simple dockerized runner you can run in your environment or we can run from our side."
06:40 Claire: "Cost target — we don't want inference to exceed $X per 1k tokens for assistant heavy flows. We'll share a target range in the prompt set."
06:49 Maya: "Okay noted. We'll model cost per 1M tokens across model variants during the benchmark and produce a spreadsheet with cost/latency tradeoffs."
07:06 Tom: "Are there any blockers for us to start the harness? We might need a quick signed NDA for us to share some internal prompts."
07:14 Maya: "We have a standard mutual NDA — I'll send it after the call. Once that's done you can drop the prompt set into the benchmark spreadsheet or S3 link."
07:24 Claire: "Great. Also want clarity: for function calling, do you expect us to build the orchestration or do you provide an orchestration runner?"
07:34 Jordan: "We provide helper libraries and small orchestrator examples for common flows (search->filter->summarize) but we don't manage customer-side DBs. We'll show a pattern that delegates the function call back to your infra for actual DB/search ops."
07:50 Marco: "Perf metrics: what's a realistic p95 we should expect on hosted? 300-700ms?"
07:56 Evan: "For short 100–200 token assistant calls on a hosted optimized path, p95 around 200–400ms is realistic depending on model and network. For longer context and larger models expect higher."
08:12 Sana: "For the KMS integration, is bring-your-own-key supported?"
08:16 Maya: "Yes, BYOK via customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we support envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS through our VPC connectors. We'll detail this in the security doc."
08:30 Claire: "Ok let's wrap with explicit next steps."
08:35 Maya: "Recap: 1) Redwood to share benchmark harness + spreadsheet + example SDK/openai-compat repo by 02/21; 2) Pelago to share prompt set and traffic profile after NDA by 02/20; 3) Run hosted benchmarks week of 02/24; 4) Run Dedicated run week of 03/03; 5) Security review and KMS validation by 02/24; 6) Decision meeting target 04/14. Any objections?"
08:58 Sana: "No objections, will review security docs as they come in."
09:05 Claire: "Sounds good. Thanks all."
09:08 Maya: "Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and the NDA. Evan will own the harness deliverable."
09:15 [call ends]

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker alignment errors and occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'K V cache' vs 'KV cache'). Integration path: prefer OpenAI-compatible endpoint for quick lift-and-shift, Redwood SDKs available for deeper integration and streaming/structured output helpers. Action items and timeline recorded above.
